checks.finding: design.md ## Architecture (lines 32-69) satisfies all three required elements: (1) top-level component boundaries via the mermaid Fixture-matrix subgraph (F1-F4) and the three test-kind nodes BI/SC/OE plus the Golden-baseline node GB; (2) integration with existing components via six labeled '.extends.'/'.compares.'/'new TEST-01x' edges into tests/install.tests.sh+tests/uninstall.tests.sh (INV-007), tests/loops/loop-inventory.json (INV-001/INV-002), tests/lib/loop-driver.sh (INV-003/INV-004), tests/loop-escalation.tests.sh and tests/loop-consistency.tests.sh (INV-005), and emit-run-record.sh (INV-006); (3) technology choices for this feature's single applicable layer via the diagram's file-extension-bearing node labels (.sh/.json) cross-referenced with ## Layer Specifications' explicit 'Frontend: N/A ... every future-task deliverable is Bash/PowerShell/JSON' and 'Infrastructure: ... described in Deployment / CI Plan' (lines 109-113), appropriate since Feature Type (line 4) declares a test-infrastructure-only package with no frontend/data layer to describe. This is far beyond a one-sentence description; the Technical Summary (lines 6-30) elaborates the same architecture in multi-paragraph detail with cross-referenced REQ/INV citations.

The ## Architecture mermaid diagram (design.md lines 34-63) declares 17 dependency edges (F1/F2/F3/F4 -> BI/SC/OE; BI -> GB; BI -.extends.-> INST; OE -.compares.-> SCHEMA; OE -.extends.-> LI/LD/ERR; OE -.new TEST-019.-> LE; OE -.new TEST-018.-> LC; LI --> LIT). Every edge flows one-directionally from fixture states -> test kinds -> extension/comparison targets; no extension target (GB, INST, SCHEMA, LI, LD, LE, LC, ERR, LIT) has an outgoing edge back to a fixture state or test kind. No cycle exists.

design.md ## Test Strategy (lines 628-710) is a 9-item ordered future-task plan covering integration test scope in detail (each item names the specific existing suite/file pairing exercised together, e.g. item 3: tests/install.tests.sh/tests/uninstall.tests.sh plus golden-baseline diff-check; item 5: loop-inventory.json + loop-driver.sh + loop-escalation.tests.sh + loop-consistency.tests.sh); acceptance test approach is covered exhaustively by acceptance-tests.md's mapping of every AC-001-AC-041 to a named TEST-NNN id, Test Type, and Test Target; concrete planned verification evidence is named throughout (capture-golden-baseline.sh, promote-golden-baseline.sh, TEST-018, TEST-019, tests/run-all.sh/.ps1, .github/workflows/test.yml); mocking strategy for the one live-external dependency (LLM generation) is explicit (item 4: 'a deterministic recorded-response injection seam...never a live model call in this gating suite'). This addresses well more than one test level, so the check's own stated failure trigger ('a strategy that addresses only one test level') is not met. Non-blocking observation: design.md does not use the literal phrase 'unit test' for the new pure comparator/collector functions (_loop_trace_emit, assert_capability_applicability, assert_event_trace) or the AST canonicalizer, relying on their exercise via the full TEST-018/TEST-019 fixture-driven rounds plus a discrete malformed-corpus fixture (security-spec.md Security Tests, item 4) for the canonicalizer's parse-failure path specifically -- this does not amount to addressing only one level and is not a basis for FAIL.
